result: Scored totals (blueprints/gap-wave2-20260923/skill-arm-ab/scored-results.json): with_skill 10/12, without_skill 10/12, difference 0. Per-case breakdown: C1 (search-first) 2/2 both arms; C2 (iterative-retrieval) 2/2 both arms; C3 (security-best-practices, SQL injection) 2/2 both arms; C4 (security-best-practices, command injection) 2/2 both arms; C5 and C6 (typesafe-ai) 1/2 both arms -- both arms answered 'Insufficient' rather than the frozen 'supported' label, with materially identical reasoning quality between arms. CORRECTED 2026-09-23: 4 of the 6 cases (C1-C4) hit the 2/2 ceiling in both arms and therefore cannot discriminate between arms by construction, regardless of whether a skill was used; only C5/C6 have any scoring headroom, and their frozen labels are contestable (below), so in practice zero of the 6 cases provide a case that could show a with-vs-without difference even in principle. Mechanically, the Skill tool was never invoked in any of the 12 runs, including all 6 with_skill trials where it was explicitly allowed and the relevant skill (search-first, iterative-retrieval, or typesafe-ai) was installed and discoverable. This resolves the ambiguity the preregistration called out (the zero score difference reflects the skill never being loaded/used, not that it was tried and added nothing) but does not answer the underlying quality question either way. Per-arm usage (corrected: previously reported as a single combined figure with input_tokens misreported as 0 and no cache_read at all): with_skill cost $1.068 (output 3587, cache_creation 121080, cache_read 136480) vs without_skill cost $0.830 (output 3487, cache_creation 90501, cache_read 178935) -- with_skill cost about 29% more, but every case ran with_skill first and without_skill second (verified by file mtimes), so without_skill's larger cache_read and smaller cache_creation are at least partly a cache-warmth artifact of run order, not an effect attributable to the skill option itself; this confound means the cost comparison cannot be attributed to 'with skill' vs 'without skill' and gap 1's cost question is not answered by this data. On reflection after scoring, C5/C6's frozen 'supported' label is contestable: a stated numeric range does not, on a strict reading, establish a specific point figure, and 'discontinued support' could plausibly mean more than 'stopped taking new requests' -- both arms' 'Insufficient' answers are defensible, and this is recorded as a preregistration weakness in this receipt rather than silently rescored.

verdict_impact.explanation: CORRECTED 2026-09-23: gap 0 is NOT settled by this receipt, only partially advanced. A frozen, separately-labeled 6-case fixture and a repeatable claude -p harness now exist and were run and scored once (procedural progress on 'no retained fixture'), but the fixture did not measure skill-arm task performance as gap 0 requires: the Skill tool was never invoked in any of the 12 trials, 4 of 6 cases hit a 2/2 ceiling that cannot discriminate arms regardless of skill use, and gap 0's own next_check also asked for a codex exec arm and per-arm provider usage, neither of which was produced (codex exec was not run in this unit; per-arm usage is now added in this fix round but was originally reported only as a single misleading combined figure). Gap 1 remains open, not partially settled with a clean null result as previously claimed: the observed zero quality difference is explained by the Skill tool never being invoked (so it is not evidence the skills fail to help when loaded), and the ~29% with_skill-arm cost difference is confounded by with_skill always running first (cache warmth), so neither the quality nor the cost half of gap 1 is actually measured here. Gap 7 is NOT meaningfully advanced, as the original receipt already noted: TypeSafe's own typed-judgment inference was never exercised since typesafe-ai was never invoked via the Skill tool.

limitations: N=1 per case per arm; single-rater diagnostic scoring by this receipt's author against a rubric frozen in advance, not blinded or independently adjudicated (labeled diagnostic per the unit's own instruction).

Because the Skill tool was never invoked in any run, this A/B does not actually test 'with the skill's guidance applied' versus 'without it' -- it tests 'with the option to use the skill' versus 'without that option', which turned out to make no observed difference because the option was never exercised either way. A prompt that forces Skill invocation (rather than merely allowing it) was not tried in this unit due to budget.

4 of 6 cases (C1-C4) hit a 2/2 scoring ceiling in both arms, so they cannot discriminate a with-vs-without difference by construction; only C5/C6 had scoring headroom, and their frozen labels are independently contestable (see below). No case in this 6-case set could, even in principle, have shown a clean measured quality difference.

Every case ran with_skill before without_skill (same order for all 6 cases, confirmed by file mtimes), so the without_skill arm's consistently higher cache_read_input_tokens and lower cache_creation_input_tokens is at least partly a cache-warmth effect of run order rather than an effect of the skill option; the ~29% with_skill cost premium cannot be attributed to the skill option alone. A randomized or counterbalanced run order was not used and is recorded as a design weakness, not corrected retroactively.
The C5/C6 frozen labels are contestable on reflection (see 'result' above); this is recorded honestly as a preregistration weakness rather than corrected after the fact by rescoring.

This receipt does NOT close gap 7. Re-examining the original 8-case set's C4 disagreement and running an actual TypeSafe-API arm against a native coding-agent baseline on an extended case set both remain open; attempting them was assessed as exceeding this unit's remaining claude -p budget and time and is recorded in the coordinator handoff as undone.
This receipt does NOT include the codex exec arm that gap 0's next_check explicitly asks for; it is claude -p only and is recorded as undone for the codex-exec half.

All 12 calls used --effort medium as instructed; the stream-json output does not expose a provider-confirmed resolved effort level, so 'medium' reflects the flag passed, not an independently verified resolution.

The original 12 claude -p calls were not re-run; per-arm usage was recomputed from the already-retained transcripts' final 'result' events (a new, additive computation, not a rerun of any model call), and settles_gap/verdict_impact/result were rewritten to remove the overclaim.
